findings.title: Reverts unconditional autoescape Environment, making stored-XSS protection dependent on a deprecated Starlette passthrough
findings.problem: This diff reverts commit e11187e, whose message states Starlette removed the **env_options passthrough, breaking autoescape=True on newer versions. The installed starlette 0.52.1 still honors the path but marks it deprecated with a DeprecationWarning. pyproject.toml pins fastapi/jinja2 with no upper bound, so a routine dependency refresh can pull a Starlette release that reproduces the regression this project already hit and fixed once.
findings.fix_hint: restore the preconfigured jinja2.Environment(loader=jinja2.FileSystemLoader(...), autoescape=True) passed via Jinja2Templates(env=...), as in commit e11187e
findings.why_it_matters: settings.html renders user-controlled config values (inst.missing_tag, inst.cutoff_tag, inst.url) with no manual escaping, relying entirely on Jinja2 autoescape. missing_tag/cutoff_tag are stored with only .strip() applied and validate_arr_url does not reject quote or angle-bracket characters. If autoescape silently reverts to off, an attacker reaching the settings form could achieve stored XSS in the admin settings page.

members.title: Keep script-injection protection off deprecated environment options
members.problem: Line 45 replaces direct Jinja autoescape configuration with Starlette's deprecated **env_options forwarding. Installed Starlette 0.52.1 explicitly warns to use a preconfigured Environment. A render probe confirms escaping works today; no current XSS bypass was demonstrated. However, the protection now depends on continued support for that deprecated path. Docker installs unbounded dependencies from pyproject.toml without uv.lock. If escaping lapses, interpolations such as entry.name and entry.detail in templates/partials/search_log.html:19 become script-injection sinks; removal of the keyword path could instead prevent startup.

members.problem: With Starlette 0.52.1 installed, Jinja2Templates(directory=..., autoescape=True) goes through the deprecated **env_options passthrough; importing triggarr.web.routes with -W error::DeprecationWarning raises. The previous commit (e11187e) switched to a preconfigured jinja2.Environment for exactly this reason, so this diff undoes that change.

members.why_it_matters: pyproject.toml lists fastapi with no version pin. When Starlette turns this deprecation into a removal, the app fails at import time or silently drops the setting. Autoescape is the project's XSS control for rendered templates.

members.title: Reverts fix e11187e: HTML autoescaping (XSS protection) now depends on Starlette's deprecated env_options passthrough
members.problem: This diff undoes the previous commit (e11187e). It goes back to passing autoescape=True through Jinja2Templates(directory=..., **env_options). Starlette 0.52.1 still accepts that path but marks it deprecated: importing triggarr.web.routes raises DeprecationWarning 'Extra environment options are deprecated. Use a preconfigured jinja2.Environment instead.' pyproject.toml lists fastapi and jinja2 with no version pin. If a later Starlette removes **env_options, the app fails at import with a TypeError; if it stops honoring the option, templates render user-controlled content unescaped. Today escaping still works because Starlette's _create_env also defaults autoescape to True.

members.title: Reverting e11187e makes the XSS autoescape guarantee depend on Starlette's deprecated env_options path, while Docker builds pull unpinned FastAPI/Starlette
members.problem: The previous code built the jinja2.Environment directly with autoescape=True, independent of Starlette. This diff routes the setting through the deprecated **env_options path (DeprecationWarning in starlette 0.52.1). The Dockerfile runs pip install . against pyproject.toml where fastapi has no version pin, so uv.lock is ignored and each image build pulls the newest Starlette. When Starlette drops env_options, either routes.py raises TypeError at import (whole daemon fails to start, since __main__.py and scheduler.py import it) or the option is silently dropped, reopening HTML injection in all 10 TemplateResponse render sites.

members.why_it_matters: The diff saves almost nothing and adds a deprecation warning on every startup. Its downside is either a full daemon outage at import or a lost XSS guarantee on every rendered page, triggered by an ordinary Docker rebuild with no code change.
